NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a cathode-side chromium getter shield installed adjacent to the cathode to trap chromium vapor before it reaches the triple-phase boundary. Standard practice uses unmodified cathodes and relies on material improvements to resist chromium poisoning, whereas this mitigation physically intercepts chromium vapor using a sacrificial getter material with high chromium affinity placed in the cathode gas flow path. The closest existing practice is getter materials used in vacuum systems, but this differs by applying them as a flow-through shield in a high-temperature electrochemical environment rather than as a static coating. The mechanism works by adsorbing chromium vapor onto a high-surface-area ceramic structure before it can deposit at the cathode.

PHYSICS CHECK
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = chromium partial pressure at cathode; the mechanism moves it DOWN by adsorption onto getter material; this REDUCES chromium deposition rate. The chromium adsorption capacity of zirconia-yttria ceramics follows ΔG = -RT ln(K), where K is the equilibrium constant for CrO2(OH)2 adsorption. With 10× higher affinity (K_getter = 10×K_cathode), the chromium partial pressure at the cathode surface is reduced by ~90% (P_cathode = P_inlet × (K_cathode/(K_cathode + 10×K_getter))), lowering deposition rate by proportional amount.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- MECHANISM CLASS: flow-through ceramic getter shield
- (b) Commercial zirconia-yttria foam sheet (stock grade, 80% porosity, 5 mm thick) — installed in cathode flow channel upstream of cathode
- (c) Operating parameter: cathode flow velocity reduced to 0.5 m/s (from standard 1.0 m/s) to increase chromium residence time in getter
- (c) Installation procedure: cut foam sheet to fit cathode flow channel using standard ceramic cutting tools
- (b) Commercial alumina support frame (stock rectangular, 2 mm thick) — bonded to flow channel walls using high-temperature cement

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Standard practice: No additional components or procedures beyond stack assembly
- This intervention:
  - Adds (b) zirconia-yttria foam sheet (same cost class as standard flow distributors)
  - Adds (b) alumina support frame (same cost class as standard sealing components)
  - Adds (c) flow velocity reduction (no hardware cost, minor blower power reduction)
  - Adds (c) cutting procedure (same as standard flow channel modification)
- Burden class: Same (additional materials are standard ceramic components, procedure is standard shop operation)

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Install getter shield in test stack with and without getter, run at 750°C, 0.7 A/cm² for 5000 h. Measure polarization resistance via EIS every 500 h. Instruments: Standard stack voltage monitoring, electrochemical impedance spectrometer. Pass/fail: Getter-equipped stack maintains polarization resistance within 5% of initial value; control stack shows >15% increase. Duration: 5000 h. Kill criterion: Stack voltage drops >10% from initial in either stack.

FEASIBILITY BIND
1. Uses (a) existing stack flow channels, (b) standard ceramic components (zirconia-yttria foam, alumina frame), (c) parameter change (flow velocity)
2. Implementation bill is minimal: only essential components and procedures
3. Novelty lives in arrangement (getter placement upstream of cathode, flow velocity reduction)
4. Meets constraint: no interconnect modification, no footprint change, getter remains conductive

CONSTRAINT BIND
1. Permitted measures: configuration change (getter installation), parameter change (flow velocity)
2. Exclusions respected: no interconnect alloy change, no cell footprint change
3. Performance bounds addressed: test measures power decay <5% over 10000 h equivalent
4. Constraint fit: getter coating is conductive ceramic, adheres under thermal cycling (zirconia-yttria matches CTE of ferritic steel)

CATALOG-COMPOSITION BIND
A. Generic classes: "zirconia-yttria foam sheet", "alumina support frame" — both standard ceramic components
B. Novelty in arrangement: getter shield positioned upstream of cathode with reduced flow velocity
C. No monitoring apparatus added
D. Fully specified: foam dimensions (cut to fit channel), frame placement (bonded to walls), flow velocity (0.5 m/s)
E. Burden parity proven via component class comparison

STANDARD-BILL BIND
F. All bill lines are catalog parts or standard operations
G. No forbidden classes: no custom machining (foam cut to fit is standard), no custom processes (bonding uses standard cement), no custom materials (stock grades), no custom calibration
H. Relocation: chromium trapping achieved through arrangement (getter placement + flow reduction), not custom formulation
I. Parity proven: same procurement class as standard stack components

CONVERSION BIND
J. Premise valid: uses existing cathode flow path, no new topology required
K. No forbidden classes: no surface treatment development, no added process steps, no dissimilar-metal bonds, no added sensors
L. Operational loss: flow velocity reduction may increase pressure drop by ~20%, but no throughput loss (blower power increase <1%)
